title: A Friction Testing-Bioreactor Device for Study of Synovial Joint Biomechanics, Mechanobiology, and Physical Regulation
protocol: Design the friction testing device on a rigid base plate for structural support.
Attach a stepper motor to the horizontal translation stage to create a two-axis friction testing device.
Mount a multiaxial load cell on the translation stage to measure normal and tangential loads.
Equip the translation stage with a linear encoder to record horizontal displacement.
Equip the loading stage with a linear encoder to record vertical displacement.
Configure the loading platen as a glass, cartilage, or synovium counterface.
Connect the platen to the loading stage via a threaded support rod.
Attach a fixed base of a two-part magnetic base to the top of the load cell.
Attach a removable base of the magnetic base to the fixed base.
Prescribe a normal load using dead weight mounted on linear bearings above the loading platen and support rod.
House the device within an aluminum-framed acrylic enclosure.
Sterilize metal tools in an autoclave.
Spray joint holders with 70% ethanol.
Place joint holders and other materials inside a biological safety cabinet (BSC).
Close the BSC for one ultraviolet (UV) cycle.
Retrieve sterilized tools from the autoclave.
Place sterilized tools, betadine, sterile scalpel blades, and beakers containing 70% ethanol in the BSC.
Open the tools and place them in 70% ethanol beakers inside the BSC.
Attach scalpel blades to scalpel handles.
Prepare the joint for harvest.
Spray the outside of the joint with 70% ethanol.
Wrap the joint in aluminum foil.
Place the wrapped joint inside the BSC after 30 minutes.
Open the foil and secure the joint to its holder.
Cover the joint in betadine by gently wiping it across the surface.
Secure the tibiofemoral joint capsule using a ring stand with the anterior side facing the dissector.
Sever the patellar tendon using forceps and a scalpel blade, making a horizontal incision of 5-10 cm superior to the tibia.
Hold the detached patella tendon with forceps.
Make two anterior-to-posterior cuts in the shape of a V to free the patella.
Rotate the patella behind or remove it completely from the joint.
Carefully remove tissue superficial to the synovial membrane on both sides of the joint.
Trace the outline of the synovium region of interest with a scalpel blade.
Grasp one end of the synovium and gently lift to stretch it distal to the bone.
Remove the synovium from the bone using a scalpel blade.
Place the tissue in appropriate culture media or testing bath solution.
Harvest juvenile bovine cartilage (femoral plugs and tibial strips).
Separate the femur from the tibia by severing the ACL, PCL, MCL, and LCL.
Place the separated tissues in their respective holders for dissection.
Secure the femur using a ring stand.
Drive the biopsy punch normal to the femoral condyle articular cartilage surface until reaching the bone.
Loosen the plug's connection to the bone by moving the punch left to right and forward to backward without removing it.
Remove the punch and the plug from the underlying bone.
Shave the deep side of the plug flat with a box cutter or scalpel if necessary for mounting onto a testing base.
Place tissue in appropriate culture media or testing bath solution.
Secure the tibia in an adjustable holder.
Remove the meniscus carefully while avoiding contact with the cartilage surface.
Use a box cutter to cut perpendicular to the cartilage toward the bone on the outer edges of the tibial plateau.
Cut completely through the cartilage to make straight edges/sides.
Begin the cut approximately 2 mm away from each tibial plateau edge and remove excess tissue.
Score the inside edges of the cartilage.
Use a box cutter to make a clean cut at the interface between the bone and cartilage on the outside edges, parallel to the cartilage surface and approximately 5 mm inward.
Gently insert a flathead screwdriver below the cut made in step 2.3.3.2.
Gently rotate the screwdriver to loosen the articular cartilage from the subchondral bone.
As the sample loosens, slowly push the screwdriver forward until the cartilage strip detaches from the bone.
Push the screwdriver toward bone, not toward cartilage.
Repeat this process at multiple locations until the tibial plateau articular cartilage is completely removed from the underlying bone.
Cut the tibial plateau surface to produce rectangular samples of desired size and thickness using a box cutter.
Place tissue in appropriate culture media or testing bath solution.
Remove the removable magnetic base and glue a 60 mm diameter Petri dish to the top surface of the removable base.
Attach the removable base to the fixed base with the Petri dish glued in place.
Mark the Petri dish to indicate a sliding direction.
Apply a small amount of cyanoacrylate to the center of the dish.
Align the tibial strip with the sliding direction of the stage.
Gently press the cartilage strip onto the dish.
Restore the removable magnetic base with attached cartilage strip to its paired magnetic fixed base in the friction tester.
Fill the Petri dish with the desired testing bath solution.
Ensure the testing bath solution completely covers the cartilage.
If a femoral cartilage plug is selected for testing, remove the removable magnetic base.
Glue a 60 mm diameter Petri dish to the top surface of the removable base if using the condyle as the bottom counterface.
Apply a small amount of cyanoacrylate to the center of the new Petri dish.
Gently press the cartilage plug onto the dish.
Restore the removable magnetic base with attached cartilage plug to its paired magnetic fixed base in the friction tester.
Fill the Petri dish with the desired testing bath solution for the plug test.
Ensure the testing bath solution completely covers the cartilage.
Remove the loading platen and support rod from the friction tester.
Select a new platen suitable for cartilage mounting if necessary.
Apply a small amount of cyanoacrylate to the platen surface.
Press the cartilage plug gently onto the platen.
Restore the loading platen with attached cartilage plug and support rod to the friction tester.
Adjust the vertical height of the loading platen such that the cartilage plug hovers over the bottom counterface.
Submerge the cartilage plug in the testing bath.
Add more testing bath solution if needed.
Remove the removable magnetic base if the synovium is used as the bottom counterface.
Glue a 60 mm diameter Petri dish to the top surface of the removable base.
Glue a custom-machined circular acrylic-silicone post of the desired diameter to the center of the dish.
Place the synovium on top of the post using forceps.
Spread an O-ring over the circumference of the synovium to secure it.
Using forceps, gently pull at the synovium to stretch tissue taught and flat beneath the O-ring.
Trim excess tissue with surgical scissors.
Restore the removable magnetic base (with synovium attached) to its paired magnetic fixed base in the friction tester.
Fill the Petri dish with the desired testing bath solution.
If the synovium is used as the top counterface, remove the loading platen and support rod from the friction tester.
Remove the existing platen and select a new circular platen suitable for synovium mounting.
Using forceps, place the synovium on top of the circular platen.
Spread an O-ring over its circumference to secure the synovium.
Gently pull at the synovium to stretch tissue taught and flat beneath the O-ring.
Trim excess tissue with surgical scissors.
Restore the loading platen (with attached synovium) and support rod to the friction tester.
Adjust the vertical height of the loading platen such that the synovium hovers over the bottom counterface and is submerged in the testing bath.
Add more testing bath solution if needed.
Insert the mounted specimens into the friction tester device.
Open the software program and prescribe test parameters: stage speed, stage acceleration, travel path (distance), and test duration.
Open the three windows in the program: Analog Data Build MFDAQ, Initialize Load PID, and Trigger Dynamic Caller.
Run the Analog Data Build MFDAQ window by pressing the Run button.
Run the Initialize Load PID window by pressing the Run button.
Navigate to the Stepper tab in the Trigger Dynamic Caller window.
Specify the acceleration, speed, and distance of the translation stage in the user input boxes.
Set the zero x-position by centering the bottom counterface underneath the top counterface.
Move the stage to the last-saved zero x-position using the Home button in the Stepper tab.
Move the stage using the green left and right arrow buttons to align counterfaces.
Click on the Zero button to save the current stage location as the new zero x-position while the Trigger Dynamic Caller window is running but before the stage begins to move.
Stop the Trigger Dynamic Caller window by clicking on the Stop button if necessary.
Repeat step 3.5.1 if the desired zero x-position is not obtained initially.
Hit the Zero button intermittently as you manually align the bottom counterface under the top counterface using the Home button to return to saved positions.
Initiate friction testing of the samples by pressing the Run (white arrow) button in the Trigger Dynamic Caller window once the counterfaces are centered and aligned.
Slowly bring the top counterface into contact with the bottom counterface after initiating cyclic movement.
Confirm applied load value by viewing the Fz real-time plot in the software window during test run.
Collect friction testing data as the test runs.
